statusText: Tail risk has moved into the watch band at 21% while Stress remains high at 78%. Mapped policy state: WATCH.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail rises from 12% to 21% because NQ has now taken out Friday's 30,679.00 low with a new 30,667.75 session low, the reopen leg from 30,920.75 has been retraced without a pullback of consequence, and several independent amplifiers align: Kospi -2.4%, Asia-Pacific ex-Japan -0.6%, NQ weaker than ES by roughly two to one, a 5.5185% 30Y yield and a 10Y at its highest since 2007. Tail is held below the 25% block threshold because the magnitude is still modest at -0.70%, the breach of Friday's low is only about 11 points, VIX closed Friday at 14.87 with no volatility confirmation, the Nikkei is little changed and WTI has eased from a $94.33 high to $93.25. The named danger window is 13:00Z-15:00Z, covering the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed release.
headline: NQ takes out Friday's low at 30,667.75 and trades 0.70% under settle with Kospi -2.4% and a 5.5185% 30Y yield, lifting Tail to the 21% watch band, while a 14.87 VIX and an unchanged Nikkei cap it below the block threshold
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,673.50 in the Monday Globex session, 215.75 points and 0.70% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement, and the shape of the move has changed materially over the past hour. Price opened the week at 30,870.00, printed 30,920.75, and has since worked steadily lower to a new session low of 30,667.75, where it currently sits about six points above that low. Two observations follow. First, the entire reopen up-leg has been retraced and the downside has extended, with no pullback of consequence across the span; that is the shallow-pullback shape that matters most to a mean-reversion framework. Second, and new this hour, the 30,667.75 low is now marginally below Friday's 30,679.00 low, so the overnight move is no longer a rotation contained inside the previous session's envelope.

The cross-asset tape has also become more aligned than it was. E-mini S&P futures at 7,775.75 are down 0.36% and also sitting at their session low of 7,773.75, so both indices are pinned at the lows, with NQ carrying roughly twice the percentage loss. That ratio points to an index-specific technology and semiconductor drag rather than a broad risk-off move, and Asia corroborates it: Reuters reports the Kospi down 2.4% and the Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index down 0.6% while the Nikkei is little changed. The rate backdrop is the named cause. The 30-year Treasury yield is quoted at 5.5185%, its highest since 2004, the 10-year at roughly 5.18% is at its highest since 2007, and the 2-year has added about 55 basis points during September; H.15 records 4.87%, 5.18% and 5.47% for the 24 September observation. Energy remains elevated, with Brent near $106.31 to $106.49 and roughly 18% higher since 1 September, and WTI at $93.25 after a $94.33 session high and a $92.41 previous close.

Four things keep Tail inside the watch band rather than at a blocking level. The magnitude is small: 0.70% net and a 253-point range on a 30,700 index. The breach of Friday's low is about 11 points, which in the thinnest liquidity window of the week is as consistent with a liquidity probe as with a genuine breakdown. There is no volatility confirmation, since VIX closed Friday at 14.87, down 5.11%. And the energy amplifier is decaying rather than building within the hour, with WTI off its high. Friday's cash session closed constructively for exactly the sector now under pressure, with SMH up 1.01%, XLK up 0.80%, Microsoft up 3.66% and Apple up 1.53%, so a confirmed reversal of that leadership still requires the US cash session to participate.

The geopolitical state is unresolved but static rather than newly escalating. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, with one recorded transit on 20 September against an 85-per-day baseline and 233 AIS-visible vessels holding position; Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day reopening roadmap, Iran's foreign minister has said Tehran is prepared for war, and the parliament speaker has said there will be no reopening until Iran's conditions are met. That backdrop is the main reason Stress stays at 78%, near the top of the high band, and it is scored as a Stress and Confidence input rather than as a Tail amplifier, because no new escalation has occurred in the past several hours and the rejection is already some nine hours old. Confidence rises to 79% on live NQ and ES pricing, live WTI, verified Brent and Treasury levels, Reuters-sourced Asian cash numbers timed near this assessment, and a verified seven-day US calendar; the shared Finviz context was read but is stale at over three hours old and marked partial, so it was not used as evidence. The named danger window is 13:00Z to 15:00Z, spanning the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, where an opening-auction continuation with failed first retracements would be the clearest conditional path to mean-reversion failure.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours are covered by published Claude assessments and none has been revised. Tail stayed inside the 6%-14% low band throughout, drifting up from 6% across the quiet Sunday hours to a 14% peak at the 23:00Z hour just after the Globex reopen, easing to 9% once the reopen round trip completed, then rebuilding to 12% by the 02:00Z hour. Stress climbed steadily from 55% to 76% as the energy and Hormuz backdrop developed. Confidence dipped to 67% in the illiquid weekend hours before recovering to 76%-79% once continuous futures pricing returned. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and only the final 02:00Z hour departed from the normal dominant mode, recording mixed.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 03:00Z hour on 28 September through 02:00Z on 29 September. Tail sits in the 20%-23% watch band for ten of the 24 hours and in the 15%-19% low band for the other fourteen, peaking at 23% for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours that contain the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed release. Those two hours carry the event/whipsaw mode, and the named structural risk for them is opening-auction continuation with a failed first retracement, which is a conditional checkpoint rather than observed structure. Tail is lowest at 15% around the CME maintenance break and across the early Tuesday Asian hours, where liquidity is thin but the information set is settled. Stress stays in the high band throughout, holding at 78% through the European and US sessions before easing to 74% overnight, and Confidence runs from 79% now down to 72% at the far end of the horizon as distance from verified evidence grows.
